originalTitle: HCLTech FY guidance stays muted despite $2.4 billion deal momentum
simplifiedContent: HCL Technologies, a technology company, recently reported its financial results for the June quarter, which were slightly better than expected. The company also announced a big investment in a new project that will help with artificial intelligence solutions. Despite this positive news, HCL Technologies didn't change its expectations for the rest of the year, which might mean its stock price won't change much for now. This is because the company is waiting to see how its clients will spend their money in the coming months. The stock price may stay steady until there's more clarity on how much clients will spend, which could affect the company's future performance.

originalTitle: Kotak's Ashok Vaswani highest-paid private bank CEO in FY26 with Rs 17.23 crore cash pay
simplifiedContent: The CEO of Kotak bank, Ashok Vaswani, was the highest-paid private bank CEO in fiscal year 2026, earning Rs 17.23 crore in cash. His pay increased a lot because of special benefits like stock appreciation rights and new options. However, when including these special benefits, the CEO of HDFC Bank, Kaizad Bharucha, actually got the highest total package. This shows that these special benefits, like stock grants, can greatly affect how much executives get paid. This is important because it highlights how executive pay is often tied to the performance of the company's stock.

originalTitle: SBI Funds raises Rs 2,663 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
simplifiedContent: SBI Funds Management recently collected about ₹2,663 crore from 129 big investors before its initial public offering (IPO) starts. An IPO is when a company sells its shares to the public for the first time. The company's IPO is worth ₹9,813 crore and is set to begin on July 14. This means that a significant portion of the IPO's target amount has already been invested by these big investors, known as anchor investors. This development is important because it shows that big investors are interested in SBI Funds Management, which could affect how the IPO goes.

originalTitle: Crude oil prices jump to one-month high after 10% rally as US-Iran war escalates; Brent oil near $85 a barrel
simplifiedContent: The price of crude oil, which is the raw material used to make gasoline and other fuels, has gone up a lot recently due to increased tensions between the US and Iran. As a result, Brent crude oil is now close to $85 per barrel, which is the highest it's been in a month. This means that the price of oil has increased by about 10% recently. The current prices are $84.98 per barrel for Brent crude and $79.79 per barrel for US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude. This matters because higher oil prices can affect the cost of many everyday things, like gas for your car.

originalTitle: Breakout stocks to buy or sell: Sumeet Bagadia recommends five shares to buy today - 14 July 2026
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market didn't move much on Monday. An expert named Sumeet Bagadia thinks now is a good time to buy certain stocks. He has picked five stocks that he thinks will do well, and he's telling people to consider buying them today. This is important because it might help investors make good choices and potentially make some money. By "breakout stocks", Sumeet Bagadia means stocks that are likely to start doing better and increasing in value.

originalTitle: Raja Venkatraman recommends three stocks for 14 July
simplifiedContent: A market expert named Raja Venkatraman has chosen three stocks that he thinks are good to invest in on July 14. He is sharing his opinion on how these stocks will perform and what strategy to use when investing in them. This means he is explaining why he likes these stocks and how to buy or sell them. This information can be helpful to individual investors who are looking for ideas on what stocks to invest in. By sharing his technical outlook and trade strategy, Raja Venkatraman is providing guidance on how to potentially make informed investment decisions.
